state.background: Review the Batch2 implementation against results/plan46/phase5/full-vitest-standard-plan.md. The user's clarified goal is to verify the behaviors the tests are meant to check; faithful reproduction of production-route execution is unnecessary. The implementation removes the Batch2 production-route Playwright/WebKit suites and their Batch2 runner/registration, while migrating the intended component contracts to Vitest Browser Mode standard APIs. The ten target component specs use Vitest page, userEvent, expect.element, expect.poll, and iframe-native DOM. They do not import Playwright Page, BrowserCommand, or use direct Playwright APIs. The SpendingBarChart quarter-filter spec checks the actual filter effect in the owning full CpiChart fixture (fewer bars then restore); its standalone test checks aria-pressed. The CPI single-year spec checks supported fixture years 2021→2021 and 2021→2022, including URL/state and chart contract. Tooltip dismissal checks chart leave and fresh custom-tooltip absence, Escape, and outside interaction with Vitest userEvent. Mobile, readability, CPI, range, and tabs assertions follow the approved plan. No production source changes remain. openspec/specs/nextjstest/spec.md has Phase5 WHEN/THEN updates, and the route-runner unit expectation now asserts the removed registration is absent.
acceptanceCriteria: The migrated specs preserve the intended in-scope user-facing component behavior, with assertions mapped to the plan's coverage table; they do not claim to verify production route, SSR/Flight, hydration, or production data loading.
The ten target component specs use Vitest Browser Mode standard APIs and iframe DOM without direct Playwright Page, BrowserCommand, or direct Playwright API usage.
Route-only Batch2 tests, commands, and registrations are removed after coverage work, while unrelated suites and the browser provider needed by remaining tests are retained.
The specification's Operational validation contracts and WHEN/THEN scenarios reflect the implemented component-test scope.
Validation evidence is accurately scoped, and the one authorized timing measurement is reported as a single component-suite run rather than a provider speedup claim.
verification: A final once-only Chromium run used Vitest v4.1.11, vitest.browser.config.ts, and @vitest/browser-playwright for the ten target files: 10 files passed and 39 tests passed; Vitest Duration was 46.08s and external wall time was 47.16s. The exact command and measurement are recorded in results/plan46/phase5/full-vitest-standard-measurement.md.

Focused CpiChart-single-year and tooltip-dismiss checks passed (2 files, 5 tests); the route-runner unit test passed (1 file, 5 tests); WebKit SectionTabsB3m passed (9 tests, 5 skipped). These are scoped checks, not additional benchmark runs.
git diff --check passed. Scoped ESLint with --no-ignore passed for affected browser specs and configuration/runner files.

Full type-check reports an error in the out-of-scope existing file results/plan46/phase4/vitest-selector-route-probe.browser.test.ts(8,33): BrowserCommands lacks inspectVitestSelectorOnProductionRoute. No Batch2 target-suite failure remains in the final run.

A read-only final diff audit found all ten target specs map to the plan, no direct Playwright Page/BrowserCommand use in them, no remaining Batch2 registration reference, and no production source changes.
knownConstraints: Batch2 production-route test coverage was removed as the plan specifies; the resulting component tests do not establish production route, SSR/Flight, hydration, production data loading, device touch, browser zoom, or iPhone WebKit behavior.
The browser provider remains @vitest/browser-playwright; the migration replaces author-facing test APIs and route-level tests, not the underlying browser engine/provider.
The full type-check is blocked by the stated out-of-scope phase4 BrowserCommands error; report this separately from the successful Batch2 browser suite.
Only one final focused suite timing run was authorized and performed; no repeat measurement or claim of provider speedup is supported.

criteria.missing_prerequisites_info: A material prerequisite is missing; identify exactly what information is needed before acceptance.

criteria.implementation_issue: A concrete implementation defect exists; identify its file/location, evidence, and correction.
